items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: like they are in J.S. Bach’s music. It’s the same vocabulary.

ctx.x: So are there wrong notes in improvising?

Well — no, no, no. It’s basically you have a choice of all 12 notes of the chromatic scale. It’s a good thing we don’t live in the Middle East where they have 48 notes and 96 notes. I mean we think we have it difficult in Europe and the Americas, and now in the Middle East where they have micro-tunings in India, it’s got to be extremely difficult and their © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

minds are just rife with information. We’ve got 12 notes, and they can all be used. But where are they used and how are they used is, at this point — at that point when you understand how to play through chord changes, the harmonies, then it’s all about not what notes all the time, but how to use the notes and where to put those notes. So in answer to your question I think that’s sort of what I did. I could play perfectly and play just the notes I need to play, but then the other chromatic tones are very…
